_note: Host-owned planning constraints for the Phase 3 research pilot. Separate from configs/phase2/host-constraints.json so the Phase 2 chain keeps binding aspp+se exactly as before. The ONE difference is the binding order: the attention gate (the real P5 card P002 / P6 candidate-P002 mechanism) is FIRST, so the runner's prefix rule makes `a` the attention gate alone and `ab` aspp + attention gate. The runner refuses any other variant name (CONTRACT_UNKNOWN_VARIANT), so the arms are the runner's own frozen vocabulary; the module set of each arm comes from this binding, never from the arm name. A patch cannot reorder this binding (the service refuses one that tries).

combination._provenance: The member list and its ORDER are host-declared (this binding's order). The per-member function names and the parameter attribution are what the combination.* mechanism checks compare the OBSERVED run against; they are declared here as the host's claim, and a mismatch fails the check. The Phase 2 constraints file records a measured record for aspp+se; this file declares the same SHAPE for attention-gate+aspp, and the first real combination probe over this member list must confirm (or correct) it. Until that probe runs, a combination result is NOT verified — which is why the mechanism check, not this file, is the gate.
combination._sharedStateNote: Empty is a claim the check will verify: the attention gate and aspp each read only their own input and return a new tensor. If either starts writing shared state, combination.shared_state fails.

_bindingScope: This binding is the Phase 3 RESEARCH pilot: attention gate first, aspp second. The Phase 2 chain reads configs/phase2/host-constraints.json (aspp + se) and is unaffected by this file. Both files pin the same required mechanism-check set; only the binding order and allowedPaths differ, and both name only host-pinned modules.
